title: A Practitioner's Guide to Graphs - Tim Ainge, Good Collective
talk_summary: Tim Ainge argues graphs are only worth building when you give the extractor a schema and ontology, then use graph-native algorithms (personalized PageRank, shortest path, subgraph matching) instead of vector search for relationship-heavy retrieval. The one hard number is a 40% reduction in code-search tool calls on a .NET codebase by retrieving subgraphs as context.

takeaways.technique: Schema-constrained extraction instead of free-form triples
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking an agent to emit subject-predicate-object triples, they hand it a typed schema (Recipe -> Ingredient -> quantity) via structured outputs, plus ontology rules (lowercase names, metric units) so nodes are consistent and queryable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: giving the extractor a schema to fill ... with consistent node and edge types, relationships become meaningful

takeaways.technique: Entity resolution before node creation (embeddings, not retrospective mapping)
takeaways.what_they_do: They dedupe near-duplicate entities (garlic vs minced garlic) at ingest time using embedding similarity rather than a naive post-hoc mapping that requires knowing all entities in advance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by using an embedding model here, we have not only more flexible matching, but we also have the ability to match on terms that we don't need to know in advance

takeaways.technique: Subgraph retrieval as agent context instead of vector/symbol search
takeaways.what_they_do: They build a code graph and retrieve the shortest path / relevant subgraph between two known nodes (e.g. checkout code and basket constructor) to hand the agent the intermediate symbols as context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we saw a 40% reduction in tool calls for code search where we used techniques like this to identify the context we needed
takeaways.numbers: 40% reduction in tool calls for code search on a .NET codebase

takeaways.what_they_do: They query for the shape of a pattern (decorator: wrapper and target implement the same interface) without knowing specific symbols, to find caching classes, anti-patterns or security issues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sometimes it's really important to be able to look for the shape of something without knowing the specific instance or node details themselves

takeaways.technique: Personalized PageRank for ranking related items
takeaways.what_they_do: Run personalized PageRank from a seed node to surface the nodes most strongly related to it in a dense graph, used for recommendations and for finding authoritative related cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some nodes will emerge with more marks on them than others. These are the nodes that have a stronger relationship with the starting node
